questions.explanation: Overjoyed means extremely happy, which is stronger than happy. Pleased, glad and content are all mild feelings.

questions.stem: What is the theme of "Night Sounds"?
options: Owls hoot loudly when it is very late
Big brothers like to laugh at camp
Fear shrinks when you understand it
Flashlights help you see in the dark
questions.explanation: When Noah names each sound, Aiden stops being scared. The owl hoots in the story, but that is a detail, not the theme.

questions.stem: How does the glossary help a reader understand "Inside a Volcano"?
options: It shows a picture of magma
It defines the two bold words
questions.explanation: The glossary gives the meaning of magma and lava, the words in bold. It does not list volcanoes or show a picture.

questions.stem: The word "autograph" is made of the Greek roots "auto," which means self, and "graph." What is an autograph?
questions.explanation: Graph means to write, so an autograph is your name written by you. A photo is not written.

questions.passage: (1) Some owls hunt for mice at night. (2) Bats fly in the dark to catch bugs. (3) Raccoons search for food after the sun goes down.
questions.stem: Which sentence would be the best topic sentence to come before sentence 1?
options: Many animals are busy at night.
My brother is scared of bats.
Raccoons can live in cities too.
questions.explanation: Every sentence tells about an animal that is active at night, so this sentence names the main idea. The sentence about owls' eyes tells only one small detail.

questions.stem: My little brother lost two baby ___. Which word best completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: The plural of tooth is teeth. You change the vowels instead of adding -s.

questions.stem: Which sentence about a holiday is written correctly?
questions.explanation: The name of a holiday, like Thanksgiving, starts with a capital letter. Turkey here is a food, so it stays lowercase.

questions.passage: (1) Last summer my family went camping at a lake. (2) We swam every morning. (3) At night we cooked corn over the fire. (4) We even saw a deer by our tent.
questions.stem: Which sentence would best conclude this story about a camping trip?
options: It was our best trip ever.
questions.explanation: This sentence wraps up the story of the camping trip. The other sentences are facts that do not finish the paragraph.

questions.stem: ___ and Grandpa planted tomatoes in the garden. Which word best completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: He is used as the subject of a sentence. Try it alone: He planted tomatoes, not Him planted tomatoes.

questions.stem: Which sentence about a party is written correctly?
options: My party is on saturday, May 9.
My party is on Saturday, may 9.
My Party is on Saturday, May 9.
My party is on Saturday, May 9.
questions.explanation: Days of the week and months of the year always start with capital letters. Party is a common noun, so it stays lowercase.

questions.passage: (1) Our school had a field day on Friday. (2) We ran races and played tug-of-war. (3) Our cafeteria has pizza on Mondays. (4) At the end, every class got a ribbon.
questions.stem: Which sentence does not belong in this paragraph about field day?
options: Our school had a field day on Friday.
Our cafeteria has pizza on Mondays.
We ran races and played tug-of-war.
At the end, every class got a ribbon.
questions.explanation: The paragraph tells about field day. Pizza on Mondays has nothing to do with field day.

questions.stem: Read the sentence: We visited Ohio last summer. Which word is a proper noun?
questions.explanation: A proper noun names a certain person, place or thing and starts with a capital letter. Ohio is the name of a state. Summer is a common noun.

questions.stem: Which sentence about where she lives is written correctly?
questions.explanation: A comma goes between the name of a city and its state. Both names start with capital letters.

questions.passage: (1) Dear Grandma, (2) Thank you for the blue scarf. (3) I wear it to school every day. (4) It keeps me warm at recess.
questions.stem: What is the main purpose of this letter?
options: to thank someone for a gift
to ask someone for a scarf
to tell about a school rule
questions.explanation: The writer already has the scarf and says thank you for it. The letter does not ask for anything.

questions.stem: Last night, Mia ___ a picture of her cat. Which word best completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: The past tense of draw is drew. Drawed is not a word, and drawn needs a helper like has.

questions.stem: Which sentence with a quotation is written correctly?
questions.explanation: The first word inside the quotation marks starts with a capital letter. Only that first word is capitalized, not every word.

questions.passage: (1) After that, she fed it some fresh lettuce. (2) Ana found a turtle in her garden. (3) First, she gave it a dish of water. (4) Finally, she let it go back to the pond.
questions.stem: Which order of sentences tells the turtle story in the order it happened?
questions.explanation: Ana must find the turtle before she cares for it. Then come First, After that and Finally, in that order.

questions.stem: Read the sentence: The turtle crawled slowly across the path. Which word is an adverb?
questions.explanation: An adverb tells how, when or where. Slowly tells how the turtle crawled. Crawled is the verb it describes.

questions.stem: Which closing for a friendly letter is written correctly?
questions.explanation: In a letter closing, only the first word is capitalized, and a comma comes at the end.

questions.passage: (1) Many fruits have lots of vitamin C. (2) ________, one orange gives most kids all the vitamin C they need for a day.
questions.stem: Which phrase best connects the idea about an orange to sentence 1?
questions.explanation: Sentence 2 gives an orange as one example of a fruit with vitamin C. However would mean the second idea goes against the first.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses a modal verb to show that something is allowed?
questions.explanation: May is a modal verb that can show permission. The other sentences only tell about leaving; they do not say it is allowed.

questions.stem: Which sentence about Ben's pet is written correctly?
questions.explanation: To show that one person owns something, add an apostrophe and s: Ben's. Likes is a verb, so it needs no apostrophe.

questions.passage: (1) It rained hard all night long. (2) ________, the soccer field was too muddy for the game.
questions.stem: Which phrase best shows that the rain caused the muddy field?
questions.explanation: The muddy field happened because of the rain, so As a result fits. The mud is not an example of the rain.

questions.stem: We stayed inside ___ the storm was over. Which word best completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: Until tells up to what time we stayed inside. Because would say the storm ending was the reason to stay in, which makes no sense.

questions.stem: I think ___ going to love this book. Which word best completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: You're is short for you are: I think you are going to love this book. Your shows that something belongs to you.

questions.stem: Diego is writing a report about how to care for a pet hamster. Which question would be best to research for his report?
options: What foods are safe for hamsters?
Why does my friend like dogs?
How fast can a cheetah run?
What color is my hamster's cage?
questions.explanation: Knowing safe foods helps someone care for a hamster, which is the topic. The other questions are not about hamster care.

questions.stem: Read the sentence: The cat slept under the warm blanket. Which part is a prepositional phrase?
questions.explanation: A prepositional phrase starts with a word like under and ends with a noun. The warm blanket has no preposition, so it is only part of the phrase.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses to and too correctly?
questions.explanation: To goes before a verb like come, and too means also. Two is the number 2.

questions.passage: (1) The hungry puppy ate its food. (2) It finished the whole bowl in ten seconds.
questions.stem: Which word is the most precise replacement for "ate" in sentence 1?
questions.explanation: Gobbled shows the puppy ate fast and eagerly, which matches ten seconds. Had and got are vague.

questions.stem: Each of the students ___ a lunch box. Which word best completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: The subject is each, which means each one, so it takes has. Students is part of the phrase of the students, not the subject.

questions.stem: Nora ___ to fix the broken kite. Which word best completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: When a word ends in a consonant and y, change the y to i before adding -ed: try becomes tried.

questions.passage: (1) Exercise is good for your body. (2) It makes your heart and muscles stronger. (3) ________
questions.stem: Which sentence would best develop the topic as sentence 3?
options: It also helps you sleep well.
questions.explanation: This sentence gives another way exercise is good for your body. Sneaker laces do not tell why exercise is good.

questions.stem: Which sentence keeps the same verb tense all the way through?
options: Sam ran home and eats a snack.
Sam runs home and ate a snack.
Sam ran home and ate a snack.
Sam ran home and eating a snack.
questions.explanation: Ran and ate are both past tense, so the sentence stays in the past. Ran with eats jumps from past to present.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses a comma correctly with the word but?
options: I ran fast but, I missed the bus.
I ran fast, but I missed the bus.
I ran, fast but I missed the bus.
I ran fast but I, missed the bus.
questions.explanation: When but joins two complete sentences, the comma goes right before but, not after it.

questions.passage: (1) Mia wore a coat. (2) It was cold outside.
questions.stem: Which sentence best combines sentences 1 and 2 using "because"?
options: It was cold because Mia wore a coat.
Because Mia wore a coat. It was cold.
Mia wore a coat because it was cold.
Mia wore a coat, because cold it was.
questions.explanation: The cold weather is the reason Mia wore a coat. Saying it was cold because of her coat gets the cause backward.

questions.stem: Which sentence is a compound sentence?
options: Jo and Max like cats and dogs.
Jo likes cats, and Max likes dogs.
When Jo got home, she fed the cat.
Jo likes cats that purr softly.
questions.explanation: A compound sentence joins two complete sentences with a word like and. When Jo got home is not a complete sentence, so that one is complex.

questions.stem: Which kind of title is usually put in quotation marks instead of in italics or underlined?
questions.explanation: Titles of short works, like poems, songs and stories, usually go in quotation marks. Long works, like books and movies, are written in italics or underlined.

questions.stem: Dev is writing a science report about frogs for his teacher. Which sentence best fits the style of a report?
options: Frogs lay their eggs in water.
Guess what? Frogs are the best!
I think frogs are kinda weird.
questions.explanation: A report uses a serious tone and gives facts. Words like sooo and kinda are too casual for a report.

questions.stem: Which sentence is a complex sentence?
options: When the bell rang, we went in.
The bell rang, so we went in.
The bell rang. We went in.
We heard the bell and went inside.
questions.explanation: A complex sentence has a part that cannot stand alone, like When the bell rang, plus a complete sentence. The bell rang, so we went in joins two complete sentences, so it is compound.

questions.stem: Which two sentences use commas correctly? Choose two.
options: We saw owls, bats, and frogs.
We saw owls bats, and frogs.
On Monday, we went to the zoo.
On Monday we, went to the zoo.
We saw, owls, bats, and frogs.
questions.explanation: Commas separate the items in a list and can follow an opening phrase like On Monday. A comma never goes between a verb like saw and the list.

questions.passage: (1) Our town opened a new pool in June. (2) The pool has three diving boards. (3) It is the most fun place in town. (4) Everyone should swim there every day.
questions.stem: Which two sentences are opinions? Choose two.
options: Everyone should swim there every day.
Our town opened a new pool in June.
The pool has three diving boards.
It is the most fun place in town.
questions.explanation: Most fun and should are the writer's feelings, which people can disagree with. The opening date and number of diving boards can be checked.

questions.stem: Which sentence about ducks is written correctly?
options: We saw brown three small ducks.
We saw small three brown ducks.
We saw three small brown ducks.
We saw three brown small ducks.
questions.explanation: Number words like three come first, then size, then color: three small brown ducks.

questions.stem: Which sentence with a question in it is punctuated correctly?
questions.explanation: The question mark goes inside the quotation marks because Ruby asked the question. No extra comma is needed after it.

questions.stem: A hexagon is split into 3 equal parts. Mia shades 1 part. Which fraction names the shaded part?
questions.explanation: There are 3 equal parts and 1 is shaded, so the fraction is 1/3. The 6 sides of the hexagon do not tell how many parts there are.

questions.stem: Which expression has the same value as (4 × 5) × 3?
questions.explanation: When you only multiply, you can group the numbers either way: (4 × 5) × 3 and 4 × (5 × 3) are both 60.

questions.stem: Noah's soccer practice ended at 5:10 p.m. It lasted 1 hour 25 minutes. What time did practice start?
questions.explanation: Go back 1 hour from 5:10 to get 4:10. Then go back 25 more minutes to get 3:45 p.m.

questions.stem: Which shows 7,045 in expanded form?
questions.explanation: 7,045 has 7 thousands, 0 hundreds, 4 tens and 5 ones, so it is 7,000 + 40 + 5. The 4 is in the tens place, so it is worth 40, not 400.

questions.stem: Which angle measure is acute?
questions.explanation: An acute angle is less than 90 degrees, so 60 degrees is acute. 90 degrees is a right angle.

questions.stem: An array has 5 rows with 9 stars in each row. How many stars are there?
questions.explanation: 5 rows of 9 is 5 × 9 = 45 stars. The number 14 comes from adding 5 + 9.

questions.stem: A hiking trail is 3 kilometers long. How many meters long is it?
questions.explanation: 1 kilometer is 1,000 meters, so 3 kilometers is 3 x 1,000 = 3,000 meters.

questions.stem: Which kind of lines never cross, no matter how far they go?
questions.explanation: Parallel lines stay the same distance apart, so they never meet. Perpendicular lines cross at a right angle.

questions.stem: Round 5.68 to the nearest tenth:
questions.explanation: The hundredths digit is 8, which is 5 or more, so the 6 tenths round up to 7 tenths: 5.7.

questions.stem: Mia has 50 beads. Each bracelet uses 8 beads. She makes as many bracelets as she can. How many beads are left over?
questions.explanation: 8 × 6 = 48, so she makes 6 bracelets and 50 - 48 = 2 beads are left. The 6 is the number of bracelets, not the leftover beads.

questions.stem: Two streets meet like the corner of a sheet of paper. What kind of angle do they make?
questions.explanation: The corner of a sheet of paper is a square corner, which is a right angle of 90 degrees.

questions.stem: Which two rectangles have an area of 24 square units? Choose two.
questions.explanation: Multiply the sides: 4 x 6 = 24 and 3 x 8 = 24. A 12 by 12 rectangle adds to 24, but its area is 144.

questions.stem: How many vertices, or corners, does a cube have? Type the number.
questions.explanation: A cube has 4 corners on the top and 4 corners on the bottom, so it has 8 vertices.

questions.stem: Which pair of numbers is a factor pair of 36?
questions.explanation: 4 × 9 = 36, so 4 and 9 are a factor pair. The pair 8 and 4 makes 32, and 5 and 7 makes 35.

questions.stem: What is 3/4 - 1/6?
questions.explanation: Use twelfths: 3/4 = 9/12 and 1/6 = 2/12, so 9/12 - 2/12 = 7/12. You cannot just subtract the tops; the fractions need the same bottom number first.

questions.stem: A box is filled with unit cubes in 2 layers. Each layer has 3 rows of 5 cubes. How many cubes are in the box? Type the number.
questions.explanation: One layer has 3 x 5 = 15 cubes. Two layers have 2 x 15 = 30 cubes.

questions.stem: Which shape is a quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides?
questions.explanation: A trapezoid can have just one pair of parallel sides. A parallelogram, a rectangle and a rhombus all have two pairs.

questions.stem: A pattern starts at 4 and follows the rule "add 5." Which statement about the numbers is true?
options: They go even, odd, even, odd
questions.explanation: The pattern goes 4, 9, 14, 19. Adding an odd number like 5 changes even to odd and odd to even each time.

questions.stem: Which describes a ray?
options: part of a line with two endpoints
a straight path with no endpoints
part of a line with one endpoint
questions.explanation: A ray starts at one endpoint and goes on forever in one direction. A part of a line with two endpoints is a line segment.

questions.stem: What is 6.4 - 2.15? Type the number.
A protractor is lined up on an angle. One ray passes through 0 and the other ray passes through 70 on the same scale. What is the measure of the angle?
questions.explanation: Read the scale that starts at 0, so the angle is 70 degrees. 110 comes from reading the other scale.

questions.stem: A triangle has sides of 7 cm, 7 cm and 7 cm. What kind of triangle is it?
questions.explanation: All three sides are the same length, so it is equilateral. A scalene triangle has no equal sides.

questions.stem: A box holds 24 crayons. A teacher buys 5 boxes and gives out 70 crayons. How many crayons are left? Type the number.
questions.explanation: 5 × 24 = 120 crayons. Then 120 - 70 = 50 crayons are left.

questions.stem: On a coordinate grid, a library is at (2, 6) and a park is at (7, 6). How far apart are they along the gridline?
questions.explanation: Both places have y = 6, so they are on the same horizontal gridline. Subtract the x values: 7 - 2 = 5 units.

questions.stem: Pens cost \$1.25 each. How much do 4 pens cost?
questions.explanation: 4 x \$1.25: 4 dollars plus 4 quarters, and 4 quarters make 1 dollar. So the total is \$5.00.

questions.stem: Round 2.346 to the nearest hundredth:
questions.explanation: The thousandths digit is 6, so round 2.34 up to 2.35. The number 2.3 is rounded to the nearest tenth instead.

questions.stem: Which expression has a value of 20?
Point M is 5 units to the right of the y-axis and 3 units above the x-axis. What are its coordinates?
questions.explanation: The x-coordinate tells how far right and comes first, so M is at (5, 3). (3, 5) has the numbers switched.

questions.stem: Which two amounts are equal to 2 gallons? Choose two.
questions.explanation: 1 gallon is 4 quarts, and each quart is 4 cups. So 2 gallons is 8 quarts, and 8 quarts is 8 x 4 = 32 cups.

questions.stem: Which two expressions mean "three times the sum of 8 and 2"? Choose two.
questions.explanation: The sum of 8 and 2 must be found first, so it goes in parentheses, and then it is multiplied by 3 in either order. In 3 × 8 + 2 only the 8 is tripled.

questions.stem: Which two shapes always have 4 right angles? Choose two.
questions.explanation: Every square and every rectangle has 4 right angles. A rhombus or a parallelogram can lean over and have no right angles.

questions.stem: What is 0.4 × 0.3?
questions.explanation: 4 × 3 = 12, and tenths times tenths gives hundredths, so the answer is 0.12. The number 0.7 comes from adding.

questions.stem: A rectangle is 8 inches long and 3 inches wide. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
questions.explanation: It folds evenly across the middle the long way and the short way, so it has 2 lines. Its diagonals are not lines of symmetry because its sides are not all equal.

questions.stem: A jug holds 4 liters of water. Ella pours out 1 liter and 500 milliliters. How much water is left in the jug?
questions.explanation: 4 liters is 4,000 mL, and she pours out 1,500 mL. 4,000 - 1,500 = 2,500 mL. 1,500 mL is the amount poured out, not what is left.

questions.stem: Pattern X starts at 0 and adds 2. Pattern Y starts at 0 and adds 8. How does each term of Y compare to the matching term of X?
questions.explanation: X goes 0, 2, 4, 6 and Y goes 0, 8, 16, 24. Each Y term is 4 times the X term. The gap is 6 only at the second terms; it keeps growing.

questions.stem: How many faces does a square pyramid have?
questions.explanation: A square pyramid has 1 square base and 4 triangle faces, so it has 5 faces. It has 8 edges, not 8 faces.

questions.stem: Which two numbers are equal to 4 × 2/3? Choose two.
questions.explanation: 4 × 2/3 = 8/3, and 8/3 is 2 wholes and 2/3 more, or 2 2/3. Multiplying the bottom by 4 as well gives 8/12, which is too small.

questions.passage:
A line plot shows the weights of pumpkins at a farm stand. Each X is one pumpkin.

| Weight (pounds) | Pumpkins |
|---|---|
| 5 1/2 | X |
| 6 | X X |
| 6 1/2 | X X X |
| 7 | X |
questions.stem: What is the difference in weight between the heaviest pumpkin and the lightest pumpkin?
questions.explanation: The heaviest is 7 pounds and the lightest is 5 1/2 pounds. 7 - 5 1/2 = 1 1/2 pounds. 12 1/2 adds them instead of subtracting.

questions.stem: What is the value of 40 - (12 + 8) ÷ 4?
questions.explanation: Parentheses first: 12 + 8 = 20. Then divide, 20 ÷ 4 = 5, and subtract last, 40 - 5 = 35. Subtracting before dividing gives 5.

questions.stem: Which two shapes are always parallelograms? Choose two.
questions.explanation: A rhombus and a rectangle each have two pairs of parallel sides, so both are parallelograms. A trapezoid may have only one pair.

questions.stem: Read the sentence. Mr. Garcia asked the class to "preview" the chapter before reading it. What does "preview" mean?
questions.explanation: The prefix pre- means "before," so preview means to look at ahead of time. One more time would be review.

questions.stem: How does Lucas feel at the end of the story?
questions.explanation: Lucas laughs very hard and calls it the best breakfast ever, so he is happy and amused. Nothing shows he is angry.

questions.stem: Which sentence is the best summary of "A Library on Wheels"?
options: A bookmobile brings books to readers
Some towns have a big library close by
Readers need a card to check out books
A bus can drive to farms and schools
questions.explanation: The article explains that a bookmobile carries books to places that have no library nearby. Needing a library card is only a small detail.

questions.stem: Read the sentence. Hana "misspelled" a word on her quiz, so she fixed it later. What does "misspelled" mean?
questions.explanation: The prefix mis- means "wrongly," so misspelled means spelled wrong. That is why Hana had to fix it.

questions.stem: Which line of the poem "Spring" is repeated at the end of each stanza?
options: Bees come buzzing, one, two, three.
Kites go up and boots come off,
questions.explanation: Both stanzas end with the same line, so it is repeated. The other lines appear only once in the poem.

questions.stem: Why do people see lightning before they hear thunder?
questions.explanation: The article says light travels much faster than sound, so the flash arrives first. It also says lightning and thunder happen at the same time.

questions.stem: Read the sentence. The bus ride to the museum was "nonstop." What does "nonstop" mean?
questions.explanation: The prefix non- means "not," so a nonstop ride has no stops. Stopping often means the opposite.

questions.stem: Which sentence best summarizes "The Star Jar"?
options: Leah learns to whistle on one special day
Leah saves good memories all year
Leah's cousin visits her on her birthday
Leah finds a ladybug and puts it in a jar
questions.explanation: The story is about Leah writing good things on stars all year and reading them on her birthday. Learning to whistle is only one of the stars.

questions.stem: What is the main idea of "Life in a Beehive"?
options: Each bee in a hive has a job
Honey is stored in wax cells
questions.explanation: The article begins by saying each bee has a job and then tells the jobs of the queen and workers. Laying eggs is only the queen's job, one detail.

questions.stem: Why does a worker bee dance when she returns to the hive?
options: To wake up the sleeping queen
To show where the flowers are
questions.explanation: The article says the dance tells other bees which way to fly and how far to go. Young workers clean the hive, but not by dancing.

questions.stem: What happens to nectar after older workers bring it back to the hive?
options: The queen eats it all at once
The bees feed it to the flowers
The bees turn it into honey
questions.explanation: The last sentence says that back in the hive, bees turn nectar into honey and store it. The queen's job is to lay eggs.

questions.stem: The words "geography" and "geology" share the Greek root "geo." What does "geo" mean?
questions.explanation: Geography and geology are both about the earth and its land. Bio is the root that means life.

questions.stem: The words "vision," "visible," and "invisible" share the Latin root "vis." What does "vis" mean?
questions.explanation: Vision is your sense of sight, and visible means you can see it. Aud is the root that means to hear.

questions.stem: How do Ruby's feelings about her job change?
questions.explanation: At first Ruby thinks the job is boring, but after helping the boy she wants to learn where every book lives. The change goes from bored to eager, not the other way.

questions.stem: What event makes Ruby change her mind about the library job?
options: Mr. Kim gives her a prize
She reads a book about whales
She finds a lighter book cart
She helps a boy find a book
questions.explanation: Ruby uses what she knows about the shelves to help a boy find a whale book. The story never says Mr. Kim gives her a prize.

questions.stem: Which lesson does "The Library Helper" teach?
options: Ocean books are the best ones to read
Library shelves are often very tall
Big books are hard to carry home
questions.explanation: Ruby's job feels boring until she sees it helps readers. Tall shelves are a detail from the story, not its lesson.

questions.stem: Which event in "Lewis and Clark" happened last?
options: The group set out by boat
questions.explanation: The group returned home in 1806, after reaching the Pacific Ocean in 1805. Buying the land happened first, in 1803.

questions.stem: The suffix -able means "able to be." Which two words have the suffix -able? Choose two.
questions.explanation: Readable means able to be read, and washable means able to be washed. Careless ends in -less, which means without.

questions.stem: How is the young fox different from the old fox?
options: She finds a way to get the grapes
She jumps much higher than him
She thinks the grapes are sour
She gives up and walks away
questions.explanation: The old fox says he would have called the grapes sour and left, but the young fox rolls a log and climbs up. She does not give up.

questions.stem: Which reason does the author give to support keeping recess?
options: Teachers need a break at recess
Lessons are too long and dull
Playgrounds cost a lot to build
questions.explanation: The author says many students find it easier to pay attention after recess. The article never mentions teachers needing a break.

questions.stem: Read the sentence. Unlike his "boisterous" older brother, Theo was quiet and calm. What does "boisterous" mean?
questions.explanation: The word "unlike" shows that the brother is the opposite of quiet and calm, so he is loud and lively.

questions.passage: (1) Zoe likes to draw. (2) Zoe likes to paint.
questions.stem: Which sentence best combines the two sentences about Zoe?
options: Zoe likes to draw, Zoe paints.
Zoe likes to draw and paint.
Zoe, she likes to draw and paint.
questions.explanation: Joining the two actions with and makes one smooth sentence. Two sentences joined with just a comma is a run-on.

questions.stem: This puzzle is ___ than the one we did yesterday. Which word best completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: When you compare two things, add -er: harder. More harder uses two comparing words at once.

questions.stem: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: Because is spelled b-e-c-a-u-s-e. A trick: big elephants can always understand small elephants.

questions.passage: (1) To wash a dog, first get it wet with warm water. (2) ________, rub in some dog shampoo. (3) Last, rinse off all the soap.
questions.stem: Which transition word best fills the blank in the dog-washing steps?
questions.explanation: Rubbing in shampoo is the step after getting the dog wet, so Next fits. However would show a change in idea.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses the correct plural noun?
options: Two gooses swam in the pond.
Two geese swam in the pond.
Two geeses swam in the pond.
Two goose swam in the pond.
questions.explanation: The plural of goose is geese. Gooses is a common mistake because most nouns just add -s.

questions.stem: Grab your coat because ___ cold outside. Which word best completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: It's is short for it is: it is cold outside. Its with no apostrophe shows ownership.

questions.stem: Kayla wants to learn what the word "migrate" means. Which source should she use?
questions.explanation: A dictionary gives the meanings of words. An atlas has maps, not word meanings.

questions.stem: The blue bike is ___, not mine. Which word best completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: Possessive pronouns like hers never take an apostrophe. She's means she is.

questions.stem: Which greeting for a friendly letter is written correctly?
questions.explanation: A letter greeting starts with a capital letter and ends with a comma. No comma goes between Dear and the name.

questions.passage: (1) Hot melted rock called magma rises from deep inside Earth. (2) When the pressure builds, the magma bursts out. (3) Once it reaches the surface, it is called lava.
questions.stem: Which sentence would make the best topic sentence to come before sentence 1?
options: I visited a museum last year.
Lava can be orange or red.
Some mountains have snow on top.
Here is how a volcano erupts.
questions.explanation: The paragraph explains the steps of an eruption, and this sentence tells the reader that. Lava's color is only one detail.

questions.stem: Which two sentences use the correct verb? Choose two.
options: The bird sing in the tree.
The birds sing in the tree.
The boys runs to the gate.
questions.explanation: A plural subject like birds takes sing, and a singular subject like sister takes plays. The boys runs mixes a plural subject with a singular verb.

questions.stem: Put the plates over ___ on the table. Which word best completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: There tells where something is. Their shows that something belongs to people.

questions.passage: (1) The runner went across the finish line. (2) She raised her arms and smiled.
questions.stem: Which word is the most precise replacement for "went" in sentence 1?
questions.explanation: Sprinted shows the runner was going very fast. Moved is true but does not tell how she crossed the line.

questions.stem: Which two groups of words are complete sentences? Choose two.
options: The puppy barked at the mail.
questions.explanation: Each complete sentence has a subject and a verb and tells a whole thought. Since the game was over has both but still needs more to finish the thought.

questions.stem: Which two sentences use capital letters correctly? Choose two.
options: Our class went to lake Erie.
Our class went to Lake Erie.
We saw the Museum on Main Street.
questions.explanation: Names of places like Lake Erie and titles with names like Mr. Lopez are capitalized. Museum is a common noun here, so it stays lowercase.

questions.stem: Which sentence says the idea in the clearest and shortest way?
options: The bus left at noon at 12.
At noon the bus left at noon.
The bus, it left at noon.
questions.explanation: Noon and 12 mean the same time, so saying both repeats the idea. In the sentence that starts with The bus, it, the word it is not needed.

questions.stem: Read the sentence: Me and Tom walked to school. Which words should take the place of "Me and Tom"?
questions.explanation: The pronoun is part of the subject, so use I, and it is polite to name the other person first. Try it alone: I walked, not me walked.

questions.stem: Which plural word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: Baby ends in a consonant and y, so change the y to i and add -es: babies.

questions.stem: Nico is writing a speech for kindergarten students about staying safe on the playground. Which sentence fits his audience best?
options: Always hold on with both hands.
questions.explanation: Young children understand short, simple words that tell them what to do. Words like vigilance and hazards are too hard for kindergarten.

questions.stem: Our garden, ___ has six rows, is full of beans. Which word best completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: Which is used for things, like a garden. Who and whom are used for people.

questions.stem: Read the sentence: When the lunch bell rang at noon we lined up. How should "rang at noon we" be written?
questions.explanation: When a sentence starts with a part like When the lunch bell rang at noon, put a comma after that whole part, before the rest of the sentence.
